# Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0511a)
**ID:** Atk S0511a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Clarifier of the Sweet Meaning
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, traditionally titled *Madhuratthavilāsinī* (or *Maduratthavilāsinī*), is the commentary on the *Buddhavaṃsa* within the Khuddakanikāya commentary collection [Phaengcharoen 2006; Endo 1997]. It provides an extensive narrative framework for the lineage of past Buddhas and Gotama Buddha, setting out doctrinal analyses such as the ten perfections (*pāramī*) [Endo 1997] and detailing the chronology of the first twenty years of Gotama Buddha's teaching career and summer retreats [Gethin 1998]. The commentary preserves notable narrative variants: for instance, it recounts only three omens seen by Prince Siddhattha before his renunciation, leaving out the corpse described in most other commentaries [Adikaram 1946], and explains that the six-colored rays emitted during the Twin Miracle derive from *kasiṇa* meditation [Zhu 2017]. In its commentarial method, it incorporates the *sambahulavāra* (manifold section), adding ten descriptive sections to the canonical *Buddhavaṃsa*'s twenty categories for each Buddha [Adikaram 1946].
DharmaNexus identifies 42,194 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 355 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual sharing is with narrative and commentarial works treating bodhisatta and Buddha biographies, especially the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* (436,569 characters shared, with an extensive parallel at §1064_1–1178 ↔ §216_0–292), the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (386,626 characters; §1064_1–1178 ↔ §213_0–289), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* (*Atthasālinī*), and the canonical *Sumedhapatthanākathā* [DharmaNexus]. Although DharmaNexus computes no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [DharmaNexus], scholars note that its itinerary of the Buddha's summer retreats corresponds closely with that found in the Chinese translation *Sengqieluocha suoji jing* (僧伽羅剎所集經) [Tournier et al.].
The Pali Text Society edition of the text was prepared by I. B. Horner, who finished editing it during the air raids of World War II and published it in 1946 [Cousins et al. 1974; Masefield 1994]. Horner later translated the work into English under the title *The Clarifier of the Sweet Meaning*, published by the Pali Text Society in 1978 [Endo 1997].
